["With Sam","It's the slack end of the watch and Sam has drawn the last of the day's water and is making it last. You ask about Mars, which you haven't before, and Sam tells you: the hum of the recyclers, the tunnel markets, spin gravity you could argue with. The telling gets specific, down to a street and the name of a shop on it. Then Sam sets the cup down. \"I left because of a scholarship that fell through at the last minute,\" Sam says. \"Since you didn't ask.\"",["Listen","Tell them about where you came from"]]

["With Sam","Sam tells you about Mars: dust storms that last a month, dome lights at dusk, everyone arguing about the future. They turn their mug a quarter turn on the table as they say it, and again. \"You'd think I'd miss the big things,\" Sam says. \"I miss the stairs.\" Then, unprompted, they say they left because of a mine closure that emptied half the town, and stop, and drink, and look at you across the mug.",["Listen","Tell them about where you came from"]]

["With Sam","Sam is in the galley with the lights down to a third, in their socks, and when you sit down they push the second mug across without asking whether you want it. You ask about Mars. \"Mars,\" Sam says. \"You want the postcard, it's too many people, real rain, and an ocean you could hear from the arcology at night. That's the postcard.\" They drink. \"What I actually left over was wanting to see a sky that wasn't painted on a dome. I don't tell people that part.\"",["Listen","Tell them about where you came from"]]

It's the slack end of the watch and Sam has drawn the last of the day's water and is making it last. You ask about Mars, which you haven't before, and Sam tells you: a hand-picked detail. The telling gets specific, down to a street and the name of a shop on it. Then Sam sets the cup down. "I left because of a debt to the wrong people," Sam says. "Since you didn't ask."

Sam is on the crate by the hold hatch, where the hull carries the drive noise and the light is bad, and moves over when you come down the ladder. You sit on the deck plate with your back to the hatch. Sam tells you about the worst day they've had on a ship, quietly, in the order it happened. A hatch number is stenciled on the frame above their head.

The observation blister holds two if neither minds the other's elbows, and Sam doesn't. The ship is dark behind you and the stars don't move. Sam is easy company. Every few minutes the hull ticks as the sun side warms.
